narrative.intro: Federal contract obligations to New Hampshire total $1.3B in FY2026 to date, delivered through 3,109 awards with an average award size of $412K. Obligations fell 56.0% year over year, and current-year totals are partial because the fiscal year is still in progress. The Department of Defense accounts for the bulk of spending at $1.1B, while other agencies each contribute much smaller totals: for example, the Department of Veterans Affairs at $24.8M and the Department of Justice at $19.7M. Vendor concentration is high: BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. received $588M and SIG SAUER INC. received $226M. Industry concentration follows defense and aerospace supply chains, with top NAICS categories including Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing at $226M and Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing at $213M. Year-to-year obligations show a peak in FY25 at $2.9B, matched by FY24 at $2.9B, and lower totals earlier and in the current FY26 at $1.3B. This snapshot highlights defense-driven spending, a few large vendors, and a partial fiscal-year picture.

sections.heading: Why did obligations fall so sharply year over year?
sections.body: Obligations fell 56.0% year over year. The current FY26 total of $1.3B is well below the most recent full-year totals of $2.9B in FY24 and $2.9B in FY25. That gap reflects a partial fiscal-year picture combined with the concentration of large awards in prior years. The Department of Defense accounted for $1.1B of the FY26 total, so changes in DoD buying drive much of the movement.

sections.heading: Where are the dollars concentrated by agency, vendor, and industry?
sections.body: The Department of Defense leads with $1.1B in obligations for FY2026 to date, followed by agencies in the tens of millions such as the Department of Veterans Affairs at $24.8M. Vendor concentration is high: BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. received $588M and SIG SAUER INC. received $226M. Industry totals center on defense and aerospace categories, with Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing at $226M and Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing at $213M.

faq.q: How much federal contract money goes to New Hampshire?
faq.a: Federal contract obligations to New Hampshire total $1.3B in FY2026 to date. That amount comes from 3,109 awards with an average award size of $412K. Current-year totals are partial because the fiscal year is still in progress.

faq.q: Which agencies award the most contracts in New Hampshire?
faq.a: The Department of Defense awards the most contracts in New Hampshire, totaling $1.1B in FY2026 to date. Other top buying agencies for the same period include the Department of Veterans Affairs at $24.8M, the Department of Justice at $19.7M, and the Department of Health and Human Services at $19.6M.

faq.q: Who are the largest federal contractors in New Hampshire?
faq.a: The largest federal contractors in New Hampshire for FY2026 to date are BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. at $588M and SIG SAUER INC. at $226M. Other top vendors include ENVISION TECHNOLOGY, LLC at $70.8M and a second BAE listing at $42.9M.
